summary: The composite starts at a midpoint of 50. Draft ceilings are added for access and subtracted for offences and mapped hazards, then clamped between 0 and 100. An input that has not been loaded is skipped. It is not treated as zero.

caveats: The weights are round numbers chosen so the arithmetic is visible. They are not fitted to sales, surveys, or claims.
An empty input is skipped, not treated as zero. A suburb with only a crime figure is not scored as if it had no schools.
Offence rates follow where people gather as well as where people live. A busy centre can look worse than a quiet street.
The composite is a reading aid. It is not a ranking of virtue, and it is not advice about where to live.
Personal weights on the match page are a second draft. They re-rank the same inputs once scores exist. They do not create new data.
